sections.label: Budget debate and fiscal approval
sections.summary: Parliament debated the Budget and COS, approved FY2023 fiscal policy and expenditure, and passed the Supply Bills.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over the last two weeks, we had close to 70 hours of debate, 58 Members spoke over the two-and-a-half days of the Budget debate and we have covered 661 cuts over seven days of the COS debate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With the approval of the Government's fiscal policy for FY2023 and the estimates of expenditure in the COS and the passing of the Supply Bills a few minutes ago, this Parliament has taken an important step forward in positioning Singapore well for the post-pandemic future.

sections.label: Economic growth and investment approach
sections.summary: Parliament endorsed attracting high-quality investments, new growth sectors, cross-border agreements, and support for SMEs through various measures.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On the economic front, we endorsed our approach of attracting high-quality investments and developing new growth sectors, such as sustainability in the tourism and transport sectors, strengthening global and regional cooperation by forging new cross-border agreements with like-minded partners in overlapping areas of interest, such as the digital economy and sustainability, to enhance market access and create new opportunities for our businesses and encouraging economy-wide innovation and extending the necessary bespoke support to help our SMEs grow into globally leading companies through various measures, including the Enterprise Innovation Scheme, SME Co-investment Fund and the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative.

sections.label: Public Service and support measures
sections.summary: Lessons will transform the Public Service and healthcare, and additional support measures were approved under the Assurance Package and GST Vouchers Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will apply the valuable lessons learned to transform the Public Service and our healthcare system to serve Singaporeans better.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We approved additional support measures under the Assurance Package and Enhanced Permanent GST Vouchers Scheme with most support extended to the lower-income families.

sections.label: Parental leave and flexible work
sections.summary: Unpaid infant-care leave and Government-paid paternity leave were doubled, and flexible work arrangements will support parents balancing work and family.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We doubled unpaid infant-care leave and Government-paid paternity leave, sending a strong signal to fathers of the need for paternal involvement when a child is born and to encourage greater shared parenting responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will also better support parents in balancing their work and family commitments, through flexible work arrangements.

sections.label: KidSTART, preschools and aged care
sections.summary: KidSTART will be scaled up nationwide, preschools expanded, aged care refreshed around preventive care, and the Elder Care Fund and MediFund topped up.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: KidSTART will be scaled up nationwide, and Government-supported preschools will be expanded.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: From babies and children, we looked to the other end of the age spectrum and committed to refresh our approach to aged care, anchored on preventive care, to help our seniors age gracefully by staying healthy, active and engaged in their communities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also topped up the Elder Care Fund and MediFund to provide targeted assistance for seniors with long-term care and healthcare needs.

sections.label: Public housing affordability and supply
sections.summary: Public housing will remain affordable and accessible, BTO flat supply increased, and priority given to younger married couples and families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Minister for National Development assured Singaporeans that we will continue to make public housing affordable and accessible, and that we will redouble efforts to deliver keys to those who have been waiting for their Build-To-Order (BTO) flats.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will increase the supply of BTO flats and give additional priority to younger married couples and families who are trying to buy their first home.

sections.label: Seven goals for wrap-up speech
sections.summary: The speaker says recent developments give him seven goals or points to make in the wrap-up speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Due to recent developments, I have seven goals to achieve today, or rather, seven points to make in the wrap-up speech.

sections.label: Agree to disagree, unite
sections.summary: The speaker says points must be articulated clearly in Parliament, and after that, people should agree to disagree and unite behind a shared agenda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We do need to articulate them as clearly as we can, forcefully, passionately, in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: But when the dust has settled, I think it is important for us to agree to disagree in areas that we do not find agreement on, but also come together, unite and support a shared agenda, so that we can move forward decisively together.

sections.label: Form versus substance themes
sections.summary: The speaker says he will work on Mr Cheng's principles and offer three themes, with his fourth point on form versus substance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Cheng shared a few principles to guide us, I will work on that, and offer perhaps, three themes, related in some ways to think about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, my fourth point is really about what are our thoughts on the issue of form versus substance.

sections.label: Right versus popular leadership
sections.summary: The speaker says he runs leadership workshops and often asks leaders whether they aim to do what is right or what is popular.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Sixth, I often run leadership and related workshops in SAF, Civil Service, social and private sectors, our universities and among the various questions I often would ask of our leaders or would-be leaders is that: do we aim to do what is right, or to do what is popular?

sections.label: Singapore's reputation abroad
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore has a strong reputation and standing abroad, which has grown stronger after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: When I work with foreign counterparts, as many of you do, when we meet Singaporeans living abroad, it is clear that we have a strong reputation and standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: If anything, it has grown stronger after the whole COVID-19 situation.

sections.label: Budget as foundational piece
sections.summary: The speaker says the base should not be taken for granted and this year's Budget is a foundational piece for better years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Yes, we cannot and should not take it for granted, but we have an incredible base to build on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: This year's Budget is yet another foundational piece to stage us for the better years ahead.

sections.label: KidSTART programme impact on families
sections.summary: The passage states that like those involved in KidSTART, the programme is evidence based and its impact on families and children will last a lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Like those involved in the KidSTART programme, and it is completely evidence based, the impact on our families and their children will last a lifetime.
